prior_failure_class_comparison.observation: 以“Asana缺乏通用SSO声明”为前提、却引用定位的旧机会已移除。新 Asana 产品组合可能造成选择复杂性的机会明确标研究假设，并引用产品组合定位，相关性合理；没有把客户困惑写成已测事实。另一个行业机会继承新增的2022年营销来源范围问题，见N01。
三家价格conditions不再复述原先未挂证据的数字、币种/周期不清等事实解释，多个失败断言改为规范撤回提示；这部分改善成立。Trello SSO仍在conditions传播有问题的核查解释，unresolved仍公开多段模型判断，包含套餐独占与无价格信息等不能直接当作事实的断言。读者可见的推理边界仍未统一。
旧Asana Help Center 64字符加载/CSS错误页已不在本报告10份sources中。来源保留获取时间，官方价格页发布日期仍未知。新增严重性更高的时间/归因问题：2022年厂商竞品营销文章被用于 supported 行业背景，没有在陈述中保留年代、厂商立场或产品范围，见N01。Asana pricing 同URL同正文被保存两次，10份来源只对应9个唯一URL。

evidence.quote:
December 21, 2022
Trello
It seems like there’s a new project management software tool or a novel productivity mobile app released every day. But new isn’t always better. You don’t want the newest collaboration tool; you want the best. Two options you may be considering are Trello and ClickUp.
Trello Enterprise
is a straightforward and easy-to-use work and project management tool. Trello’s user-friendly environment is not only a favorite among small teams but also for large corporations. Don’t just take our word for it: 80% of Fortune 500 companies use Trello for collaboration.
ClickUp is a more complex platform that may provide additional advanced functionality that some teams would find handy. However, the extra features may create a tradeoff in the form of additional expense and ramp-up time that could lead to a delayed return on investment (ROI) for some enterprises.
Let’s take a look at Trello vs. ClickUp and discuss the four ways Trello Enterprise may be able to provide your company with a faster ROI.

interpretation: Improved retrieval hygiene, Asana SSO recognition and withdrawal of several unsupported assertions are observable. More evidence items (4 to 13) is not equivalent to better factual quality: all three prices remain unusable, two SSO questions remain unresolved despite source evidence, and the newly supported industry assertion introduces a material product/date/attribution error. Do not claim semantic pass or public research completion quality from run completion.
limitations: One revised public pilot with additional tool calls; not a controlled architecture comparison or proof of improvement caused by any single code change.
Snapshot review only; no fresh validation of vendor prices or historical marketing statistics.
